# x402 over Tari Ootle (Sapient fork)

> A payment rail implementing the x402 pay-per-request protocol over Tari Ootle: a
> Sapient (chironbuilds/tari-wallet) fork gains an x402 quote envelope and a sign-only
> claim mode, the Ootle indexer acts as settlement facilitator (hold-then-broadcast),
> and a zero-dependency client package drives the flow. Both scenarios (happy path and
> forced refund) are live-verified on the esmeralda testnet.

Branch: `x402/quote-and-signonly` on https://github.com/potr3288/tari-wallet
(base: chironbuilds/tari-wallet @ e2f7bf9, 0.6.17). Key commits: 8828a7a (envelope +
honest capability), 6f24c8c (e2e harness), e82cf1c (SDK key-order workaround +
facilitator dry-run removal), b2e2321 (refund harness fixes), 1b96487 (honesty
semantics), aee37c8 (dApp doc + foundation cross-check), 136ba44 (v2-response
detection), d920e07 (docs for it).

## Docs

- docs/x402-facilitator.md: the settlement interface spec (the whole contract). POST
  /x402/settle idempotent on `localDigest`, GET /x402/settlement/{digest}, hold →
  broadcast → confirmed/expired state machine, nine-cause error contract, validation
  checklist, confidentiality rule (no preflight may see the preimage), and a trust &
  honesty-semantics section (HTLC = client backstop, indexer hold power disclosed).
- docs/integration/x402.md: dApp-facing guide. The 402 quote envelope fields, the
  pay/settle/refund flow, and a field-by-field alignment table against the x402
  foundation repo's v2 specification, including the four deliberate wire deviations
  and the implemented v2-response detection.
- docs/integration/transaction-requests.md: the create/approve/submit transaction-request
  flow both new kinds use (reload-resume, no programmatic approval).
- packages/x402-elim/README.md: the client package (x402-elim) — pay402()
  fetch wrapper, pay(), settle(), refund on expiry, error taxonomy.
- e2e/harness/README.md: the live-testnet harness (real popup approvals, deterministic
  wallets, frozen-facilitator refund scenario) and the local facilitator stand-in.

## Wire shape (short version)

On 402 the server sends `PAYMENT-REQUIRED: <JSON>` with the flat quote envelope:
resourceUrl, resourceSha256?, amount (raw base units), resourceAddress, claimantAddress,
hashLockHex (64-hex SHA-256 of the claim secret), refundEpoch, facilitatorUrl,
facilitatorPubKeyHex?, expiresAt (ms), maxFee?. The refund leaf is AfterEpoch(refundEpoch)
and is STRICT: spendable at refundEpoch + 1, not at refundEpoch. The claim leaf is
BeforeEpoch(refundEpoch), so the quote convention is validUntilEpoch = refundEpoch − 1.
Foundation x402 v2 responses (base64 PaymentRequired with accepts[]) are PARSED when they
carry a payable Ootle entry: pay402() decodes the base64 header, selects the accepts[] entry
with scheme "exact" + the Ootle extra keys (hashLockHex/refundEpoch/facilitatorUrl) and a
recognized paymentFlow ("upfront"/"escrow"), and normalizes it onto the flat envelope — so a
v2 server that emits the Ootle terms in extra is fully payable. A v2 response with no such
entry still throws X402UnsupportedVersionError (spec §6.1: skip entries you cannot pay).

## Settlement ordering (merchant-initiated hold-then-broadcast)

Fund (x402Pay → htlcFund) → merchant signs claim (x402SignClaim, sign-only, status
signed-unbroadcast) → merchant POSTs /x402/settle → facilitator validates against its
own chain index and HOLDS → merchant serves the resource → merchant confirms →
facilitator broadcasts. If never broadcast, the funder recovers via htlcRefund after
refundEpoch (chain-enforced; live-verified). Residual risk, documented: a merchant that
claims and broadcasts without serving cannot be stopped at the payment layer — same as
ETH x402's "paid but no 200".

## Wallet surface

- x402Pay: validates the envelope (distinct actionable errors per failure), executes as
  an htlcFund, returns commitment + conditions + outputMask (the refund path is
  load-bearing — clients must persist it).
- x402SignClaim: build/sign/seal the HTLC claim WITHOUT broadcasting
  (src/background/x402SignOnly.ts). History records it as signed-unbroadcast. Popup copy
  says explicitly: "Sign only — not submitted to the network."
- tari_getCapabilities: signOnly: isLocal (honest; verified live; does not claim delivery
  proof or facilitator honesty).

## Testing

278 extension tests + 34 client-package tests + 24 facilitator-standin tests, typecheck
and build clean. Live e2e on esmeralda: happy path PASS (claim tx 21257dd3cb0e…891a0b2
finalized Commit) and refund PASS (facilitator frozen, refund tx 52a51a16ee86…ec9f1
finalized Commit at epoch 12759 = refundEpoch 12758 + 1).

## Upstream-relevant SDK findings

1. @chironbuilder/ootle-sdk verifyHtlcTerms is key-order sensitive (raw JSON.stringify
   comparison vs storage-canonicalized trees) — worked around via
   canonicalizeRelayedConditions(); upstream should canonicalize.
2. htlcClaim is submit-wired end to end; sign-only flows need the pipeline minus submit
   (buildScriptPathWitness + buildStealthTransferStatement + TransactionBuilder →
   resolve → sign → seal all work at 0.1.30).
3. AfterEpoch(N) semantics are strict (spendable at N+1) — worth documenting.
4. sendPrivately outputs are not view-key scannable; recipientCommitment must be
   delivered out of band.
